NEW LINE, tier 2: the US Treasury's cash buffer measured in DAYS OF ITS OWN OUTFLOWS. Round 11 had filed the Treasury General Account as unscoreable, and on the BALANCE that verdict was right — routine single-day swings run to $121bn, the level regime moved by trillions after 2020, and tax dates impose a calendar rhythm this repo has no machinery to remove. The READING was changed instead of the verdict: closing balance divided by the trailing 20-business-day mean withdrawal. That normalizes level, regime and most of the calendar at once, and it is not a statistical convenience — a buffer is only large or small relative to what is being spent, so when outflows spike the buffer really is shorter and the line falls without the balance moving at all. THE GUARD BECOMES VISIBLE RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Treasury says it targets about a week of outflows, and the median of the served history is 5.3 business days. The leak is sharp — the June-2023 X-date reads 0.21 days, and 72 days of 2023 sit below 3.0. Keyless, business-daily, T+1 publication, obs_date set from record_date because the source republishes across weekends. A FIELD TRAP is recorded in the module because a fetcher written from the schema alone ships broken: close_today_bal is the literal string 'null' on every modern row and the value lives in open_today_bal — verified against live responses. Both sides of the ratio are stored as components, because a ratio destroys its own inputs and this project has already paid for that lesson at the chokepoint sum.

TWO OF ROUND 11'S CANDIDATE CLAIMS WERE WRONG, AND THE PATTERN MATTERS MORE THAN EITHER. On fed_srf_takeup round 11 recorded 'calm ~$0-2B' and 'needs QUANTUM floor'. Probed properly: the calm median is $1 MILLION — three orders of magnitude out, and anyone sizing a threshold from that sentence would have built a line that never fires — and the QUANTUM floor is not the fix but the opposite. Replaying this repo's own normalize over the 1,251-day SRF era measures both options: with no floor Qn is exactly zero on 79.4% of windows (blind four days in five, against the 23% that got sofr99_dispersion rejected); with QUANTUM=1 at the source's true $1m resolution it fires 174 times in 1,241 days, twenty-one of those on $4 million of take-up against a $500bn facility. The line is blocked, not built. Symmetrically, round 11 filed tga_balance as unbuildable and it turned out to be buildable once the reading changed. THE PATTERN: all three round-11 candidate entries came from one reconnaissance pass each, and all three were wrong in a load-bearing way — one verdict inverted, one calm regime off by 1000x, one design missing. A candidate is not characterised until something has replayed the instrument's own scoring over its actual history. That is now the bar for any Backlog entry claiming 'build-ready'.

EU GAS STORAGE IS DECLINED ON SOURCING ETHICS, NOT ON DATA. The design survives probing and is worth keeping: a raw storage-fill percentage is dominated by the seasonal injection cycle, so the honest reading is the weekly fill change MINUS the seasonal-normal weekly change — did the EU lose ground against its own refill path this week. AGSI+ carries it cleanly: daily since 2011-01-01, 5,693 rows, zero missing days, and today it reads -0.61 pp/week against a level 15.5 points behind its same-day-of-year normal, which is exactly the split the design predicts (a line correctly saying 'not getting worse this week' about a situation that is already bad). But the API requires a free REGISTERED key, and the only keyless path that works is a spoofed browser User-Agent. This project does not ship that. The service asked for a registration; evading it with a fake identity is not a practice an instrument about honesty can hold, and the fact that it would work is not an argument. One human step unblocks it: register at agsi.gie.eu, add AGSI_KEY to repo Secrets.

I DELETED A PUBLISHED ROW, AND THE WAY I DID IT IS THE POINT. Re-running the IODA seed to apply the QUANTUM floor, I first copied data/archive/net_outages_preseed.csv over the live file. That archive was captured at the moment of the FIRST seed — before the 2026-08-04 daily run — so restoring it discarded the 08-04 live reading (1 country, Burkina Faso, sampled 00:53:15Z) before the merge could ever see it. Recovered from git (94d53e2) and re-scored; the row is back and the file holds 1,647 rows. THE RESTORE WAS NEVER NECESSARY: seedlib.merge preserves every published row and imports only observations no row already carries, so a seeder is idempotent — re-running it would have applied the floor and kept the live row. I built that property, wrote 'a seed may deepen the record, never edit it' in the commit message, and then went around it by hand. This is the third injury at the same seam (the first seed's merge rule, the un-forwarded QUANTUM, now this), and all three came from the seeder path rather than the collector. The property is now asserted by a test and the hazard is named in seedlib.rerun_is_safe: the seeders never ask for a restore, nothing in that module does one, and it must not be done by hand.

RE-SCORED UNDER TODAY'S RULES via the new tools/rescore.py: 34 verdicts change, all of them no-spread -> scoring, because the seed had been written without the QUANTUM=1 floor the line declares. Every row keeps its date, raw value and prose; only the verdict fields are recomputed, oldest-first, through collect.score_row with the module's own scoring_attrs. Pre-rescore file archived. THE TOOL DRAWS THE LINE IT LIVES BY: a scoring CHANGE applies forward-only and never rewrites (that is what STABLE_SINCE is for); a scoring BUG — rows judged by rules that were already declared and simply failed to reach them — is a misfire, not a verdict, and correcting it under archive-and-annotate is right. This is the second time the second case has been real, both at the seeder seam.

SETTLED TO A COMPLETED D-1 WINDOW (v3). The live fetcher now counts the outages in the last COMPLETE 24h window ending 22:00:00Z at least a day old, not a trailing window ending at collection time. The trailing window's final hours sat inside IODA's ~24h detection latency, which retimes and inflates the count: on 2026-08-24 the live read was 12 countries (z=4.69, a tier-1 FALSE ALARM) while the completed window settles to 4 (Cape Verde, Gabon, Syria, Tunisia). Adjudicated R23.1 by a five-angle re-query: 10 of the 12 were single ~40-min ping-slash24 events with onsets synchronized inside a 20-min window across four ocean basins, no BGP, cleared in 24h — a common-mode active-probing artifact, not a world event. Settling removes that whole latency-injection class and aligns the live tail with the seed (which already fetched each day at 22:00Z, i.e. 97% of the record was already this definition), so replay stays 0-divergence and STABLE_SINCE is untouched. Rows 2026-07-10 -> 2026-08-25 are the unsettled trailing-window stretch and hold the 08-24 artifact row, kept forward-only (the raw 12 is the v2 instrument's true reading, not a bug); the switch day carries a one-time ~24h window overlap. Cost: ~1-day lag, was zero-lag, inside the tier-1 freshness bar. monitor_swept thresholds unchanged.

THE SETTLE CLAIM WAS OVERSTATED — settle stabilizes the count, it does not filter the artifact. The 2026-08-25 method row said settling 'removes that whole latency-injection class'. The reconciliation tool's first-run seam audit (2026-08-26) showed otherwise: the 08-24 twelve-country synchronized-onset cluster is a stable set of IODA ping-slash24 events around 2026-08-23 01:00Z, so it lives in the SETTLED window ending 2026-08-23 22:00Z (the same twelve countries — Cambodia, Cape Verde, Indonesia, Japan, Maldives, Mexico, Myanmar, New Zealand, Singapore, Thailand, Tunisia, Viet Nam), while the window ending 08-24 22:00Z holds only the four genuine survivors (Cape Verde, Gabon, Syria, Tunisia). Settle relocates the cluster to its true date and makes the count stable and reproducible; it does not recognize it as an artifact. A FUTURE synchronized-onset common-mode cluster would therefore alarm on its own date under settle — the same tremble the trailing window would have produced, now correctly timed and stable, not eliminated. The 08-24 row itself does not reappear (past days are not re-recorded). So the class stays DETECT-AND-ADJUDICATE: the reconciliation tripwire (tools/reconcile_net_outages.py) flags such a settled tremble, the R23 five-agent re-query playbook attributes it, as 08-24 was. Settle remains worth keeping for the count stability and seed-alignment it does deliver; the overstated part is corrected here, not reversed.

SAMPLE-HOUR FIXED AT 22:30Z BY SLEEP-TO-TARGET (R25.1). flights is a concurrent SNAPSHOT scored against a baseline built at a fixed hour; aircraft aloft swing ~150/hour (~0.9z) around the target, so a mistimed sample measures the diurnal cycle, not the world. The GitHub-Actions daily cron was delayed by queue latency into the trough — the 2026-08-28 z=-3.05 tremble was a run sampled at 05:54Z, adjudicated R25 as a false alarm (the intraday sampler read 1660 at 22-23Z the same day). FIX: the daily workflow now schedules early (18:00Z) and SLEEPS to 22:30:00Z before collecting; because GH queue delay is one-sided (always late, never early, measured +0.44h to +7.91h over 34 days), the sample lands on target whenever the delay is within the 4.5h head-start (all 31 non-trough days). 22:30Z is the historical effective sample hour (the record's samples cluster there, min 22:26), so the baseline is continuous — no reseed. A backstop guard (collect.py apply_sample_guard, declared via flights.SAMPLE_TARGET_UTC_H=22.5 / SAMPLE_TOL_H=1.5) darks any reading still sampled more than 1.5h off target on a run delayed past the sleep window (rare, ~1/34). The guard is a COLLECTION-time decision frozen into the stored raw as dark, never a scoring attr, so replay stays 0-divergence and STABLE_SINCE is untouched. Weekday de-cycling is orthogonal to hour-of-day and could not touch this. The 3 pre-fix off-hour rows (08-27/28/29) stay forward-only. Simulated over the 34-day record: 31/34 days land exactly at 22:30Z, the 08-28 false tremble darks, the other two troughs sample near-target and score without trembling, and no clean day newly darkens.

SEEDED with pre-launch history, and published verdicts re-judged against it. The line went live cold on 2026-07-23 holding 20 observations against a 90-observation window, while every sibling line was seeded at birth and this one was not. 95 observations (2026-03-02..2026-07-21, row dates 2026-03-03..2026-07-22) were imported from the HKMA Open API's own range query via tools/seed_hkma.py and seedlib, taking the file from 43 to 138 rows, 105 of them scored. THE COST OF THE COLD START, measured: on 2026-08-09 the 10-observation window put Qn at 32.20 where the seeded window puts it at 112.99, a scale 3.5x wider, so the same reading of 54646 HK$m scored 19.223 and now scores 6.186 - still above the 3.000 bar, so that move was real, but its magnitude was an artifact of a window too thin to know what this series normally does. WHAT MOVED: verdict columns on 20 of the 43 published rows - 10 re-judged, and 10 that were warming-up receive a first z and become scoring. Direction moved on 14 rows. Trembling moved on none. No published date, raw_value, obs_date or source_note changed: all 43 rows are byte-identical in those four columns, verified against the pre-seed copy kept at data/archive/hkma_aggr_balance_preseed.csv. WHAT WAS NOT RECOVERED: the 11 observations lost to dark days between 2026-07-30 and 2026-09-02 stay lost. The seed stops at 2026-07-22, the day before the line launched, so no import can reach a date the published record already occupies; under seedlib's default row-date mapping three of them (2026-08-10, 08-17, 08-24) would have overwritten published stale-republish rows.
